sections.content: A dead car battery is one of the most common vehicle emergencies in India — and one of the most stressful if you don't know what to do. This guide gives you the complete, safe procedure for jump starting a car, specific precautions for modern vehicles with sensitive electronics, and clarity on when to call a professional instead of attempting it yourself.
What You'll Need to Jump Start a Car

items: A set of jumper cables (minimum 6-gauge, preferably 4-gauge) OR a portable lithium jump starter pack
A working vehicle with a charged battery (same or larger voltage — 12V for all standard Indian cars)

sections.content: The Correct Order to Connect Jumper Cables — Never Get This Wrong
The order of connection is critical. Connecting in the wrong sequence can cause sparks near the battery, blow fuses, or damage the ECU. Follow this exact sequence every time:

items: Step 1: RED cable → POSITIVE (+) terminal of the DEAD battery
Step 2: RED cable → POSITIVE (+) terminal of the GOOD battery
Step 3: BLACK cable → NEGATIVE (–) terminal of the GOOD battery
Step 4: BLACK cable → UNPAINTED METAL ENGINE COMPONENT on the dead car (NOT the negative terminal of the dead battery)

sections.content: Why connect the final black cable to metal, not the dead battery's negative terminal? Batteries emit hydrogen gas. Connecting to the terminal creates a spark risk near the gas. Connecting to a metal engine part grounds the circuit safely away from the battery.
After Connecting — Starting Procedure

Once cables are connected correctly, start the working car and let it run for 3–5 minutes. This allows some charge to transfer to the dead battery. Then attempt to start the dead car. If it starts, immediately disconnect cables in REVERSE order: black from metal, black from good battery, red from good battery, red from previously-dead battery. Drive for at least 20–30 minutes to allow the alternator to recharge the battery.
Modern Cars and Jump Start Risks

Cars manufactured after 2015 — including the Hyundai Creta, Kia Seltos, Tata Nexon, Maruti Baleno, and virtually every other modern Indian car — have complex electronics including multiple ECUs, ADAS systems, and sensitive sensors. A voltage spike from improperly connected cables or a faulty booster can damage these systems and cost ₹10,000–₹50,000 or more to repair. This is why Fiixup uses professional lithium booster packs that deliver regulated, spike-free current.
When NOT to Jump Start — Call a Professional Instead

items: The battery case is visibly swollen, cracked, or leaking — this indicates internal failure and the battery could rupture
You smell a strong sulphuric (rotten egg) odour near the battery
The battery has visible corrosion covering the terminals — clean first or call for help
Your car has a Stop-Start system (auto start-stop feature) — these require special procedures
The car attempted multiple failed starts in quick succession — the starter motor needs rest

sections.content: One of the most common questions bike owners ask is: 'How often should I service my bike?' The answer varies by brand, model, usage pattern, and city. This guide gives you exact service intervals for every popular Indian bike — so you never miss a service again.
Honda Activa (5G, 6G, 7G) Service Schedule

First service: 500–750 km (free at dealership). Second service: 3,000 km or 3 months. Regular interval thereafter: Every 3,000 km or 3 months, whichever comes first. Oil: 10W-30 SL grade mineral oil (Honda recommended). Air filter: Clean every 6,000 km, replace every 12,000 km. Spark plug: Replace every 12,000 km. For heavy city use in stop-and-go Bengaluru or Chennai traffic, shorten oil interval to every 2,500 km.
Royal Enfield (Classic 350, Meteor 350, Himalayan, Hunter 350) Service Schedule

First service: 500 km. Second service: 3,000 km. Third service: 6,000 km. Regular interval: Every 5,000 km after the third service. Oil: 15W-50 SAE grade (Royal Enfield Genuine Oil strongly recommended). Chain: Inspect every 1,500 km, lubricate every 700–800 km. Filter: Replace every 10,000 km. Royal Enfield bikes produce more vibration than Japanese bikes — more frequent nut-and-bolt tightening checks are recommended (every 5,000 km).
Bajaj Pulsar (150, NS160, NS200, Dominar 400) Service Schedule

Pulsar 150/160: Oil every 3,000 km, 20W-40 grade. Pulsar NS200: Every 4,000 km, 10W-40 semi-synthetic recommended. Dominar 400: Every 5,000 km, 15W-50 or 10W-50 semi-synthetic. All Bajaj bikes benefit from air filter cleaning every 6,000 km and spark plug inspection every 8,000 km.
KTM (Duke 200, Duke 390, Adventure 390) Service Schedule

First service: 1,000 km (critical — do not skip). Regular interval: Every 5,000 km. Oil: 10W-40 fully synthetic (Motorex or equivalent recommended by KTM). KTM engines are high-revving and heat-sensitive — use only recommended synthetic oil and never stretch intervals. Coolant: Check every 5,000 km, change every 2 years. Chain: Clean and lubricate every 500–700 km — more frequently if riding in rain.
Yamaha (FZ-S, R15 V4, MT-15, Fascino 125) Service Schedule

Yamaha FZ-S: Every 4,000 km, 10W-40 semi-synthetic. Yamaha R15 V4: Every 4,500 km, 10W-40 fully synthetic. Yamaha MT-15: Every 5,000 km, 10W-40 semi-synthetic. Yamaha Fascino 125: Every 3,000 km, 10W-30 mineral. Yamaha's Blue Core engines are fuel-efficient but require clean air filters — service every 6,000 km.
TVS (Apache RTR 160/200, Ntorq 125, Jupiter) Service Schedule

TVS Jupiter/Ntorq 125: Every 3,000 km, 10W-30 mineral. TVS Apache RTR 160: Every 3,000–4,000 km, 10W-30 or 10W-40. TVS Apache RTR 200 4V: Every 4,000 km, 10W-40 semi-synthetic. Apache RTR series benefits from an oil analysis — if oil turns very dark quickly, consider switching to semi-synthetic.
City vs Highway Riding: How It Affects Service Intervals

City riding — especially in Bengaluru and Chennai with heavy stop-and-go traffic — is significantly harder on engines than highway riding. The engine runs at idle for extended periods, building up heat without the cooling effect of moving air. Short trips don't allow the engine to fully warm up and burn off moisture that accumulates in oil. If you ride primarily in city traffic, use the lower end of your service interval range. If you primarily ride highways, you can comfortably use the upper end.

sections.content: In an Indian summer — especially in cities like Chennai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, and Mumbai — a car AC that stops cooling isn't just uncomfortable. It's a safety issue. This guide covers the 8 most common causes of car AC failure in India, how to diagnose each one, and which solutions you can address with a mobile service vs what needs a workshop.
Cause 1: Low Refrigerant Gas (Most Common)

Refrigerant is the working fluid of your AC system. Over time, every AC system loses a small amount of refrigerant through micro-leaks in seals and fittings. When gas level drops below a threshold, cooling capacity falls dramatically. Symptoms: AC blows slightly cool air instead of cold, takes much longer to cool the cabin, compressor clicks on and off rapidly. Solution: Professional refrigerant recharge (re-gassing). This can be done at your doorstep by Fiixup — we carry R-134a (for pre-2017 cars) and R-1234yf (for newer models).
Cause 2: Dirty or Clogged Cabin Air Filter

The cabin air filter cleans air entering the car's AC system. In dusty Indian cities, it clogs up faster than the manufacturer's recommended interval suggests. A clogged cabin filter restricts airflow — the AC works fine but can't push enough cold air into the cabin. Symptoms: Reduced airflow from vents, musty or dusty smell when AC is on, AC seems to cool less than before. Solution: Cabin air filter replacement. This is a 15-minute job doable at home or by a Fiixup technician.
Cause 3: Faulty or Weak AC Compressor

The compressor is the heart of the AC system — it pressurises the refrigerant to enable cooling. Compressor failure is the most expensive AC repair. Symptoms: Loud clicking or grinding when AC is switched on, AC not cooling at all (even with correct gas level), compressor clutch not engaging (you can see this with the bonnet open). Solution: Compressor replacement — requires a workshop. A Fiixup technician can diagnose the compressor health at your doorstep and advise whether replacement is needed.
Cause 4: Dirty Condenser

The condenser sits at the front of the car, behind the radiator grille. In Indian cities with heavy dust, construction debris, and insects, the condenser gets blocked over time, reducing its ability to dissipate heat. Symptoms: AC cools well at speed but not at idle or in traffic. Solution: Condenser cleaning — a compressed air or water flush that a mobile technician can do at your doorstep.
Cause 5: AC Refrigerant Leak

A refrigerant leak means the AC system loses gas faster than normal. This is different from the normal slow leakage — a leak can drain gas in days or weeks. Causes include damage to AC lines from a road debris impact, deteriorated seals, or a damaged condenser or evaporator. Symptoms: AC suddenly stops cooling after recently being serviced, visible oily residue near AC connections or condenser. Solution: UV dye leak test to locate the exact leak, seal repair or component replacement.
Cause 6: Electrical Issues — Fuse, Relay, or Wiring

A blown AC fuse or faulty relay prevents the compressor from engaging. Symptoms: AC fan blows air but not cold, compressor clutch doesn't engage, sudden AC failure after a car wash or flood. Solution: Fuse check (you can do this yourself with the fuse box cover map) or relay replacement — both are quick and inexpensive.
Cause 7: Evaporator Issues

The evaporator sits inside the dashboard and cools the air before it enters the cabin. It can develop leaks, ice over (in rare cases), or get clogged with mould in humid climates. Symptoms: AC works initially then stops cooling after 10–15 minutes (icing), musty smell that persists even with clean cabin filter, very cold air for a few minutes then warm air. Solution: Evaporator cleaning or replacement — requires partial dashboard removal and is a workshop job.
Cause 8: AC Mode Stuck or Climate Control Error

Modern cars with climate control systems can have software or sensor errors that cause the AC to not function correctly. Symptoms: Temperature display doesn't match actual cabin temperature, AC blows cold even when set to warm, or vice versa. Solution: OBD2 scan to read any AC system fault codes, followed by recalibration or sensor replacement.

sections.content: Royal Enfield motorcycles are beloved for their character, community, and riding experience — but they require more careful and frequent maintenance than most Japanese bikes. This guide is specifically for RE owners in Bengaluru, covering everything from service intervals and oil selection to common problems and the real cost comparison between authorised service centres and Fiixup's doorstep service.
Royal Enfield Service Schedule: Complete Interval Guide

New Royal Enfield bikes have specific mandatory service intervals to maintain warranty. First service at 500 km — free at authorised dealer, critical for engine break-in. Second service at 3,000 km — oil change, chain, filters, all checked. Third service at 6,000 km — full inspection, valve clearance check. After third service: every 5,000 km or 6 months, whichever comes first. For heavy city use in Bengaluru traffic, reduce interval to every 4,000 km.
Which Engine Oil for Royal Enfield? Complete Guide

Royal Enfield recommends 15W-50 SAE grade oil for all its 350cc and 650cc models. Royal Enfield Genuine Oil (their own brand) is strongly recommended but not mandatory for non-warranty models. Alternatives: Motul 7100, Shell Advance Ultra, Castrol Power 1 Racing — all 15W-50 fully synthetic are acceptable for post-warranty bikes. Avoid using 10W-30 or 10W-40 oils in RE engines — these are too thin for the higher clearances in Royal Enfield engines and cause more oil consumption and wear. Change frequency: Every 3,000–5,000 km depending on riding conditions.
Common Royal Enfield Problems in Bengaluru

Royal Enfield Classic 350, Bullet 350, and Meteor owners in Bengaluru frequently encounter these issues. Chain wear: RE bikes have heavier chains that stretch faster. Inspect every 2,000 km, lubricate every 700 km. Bengaluru's monsoon causes rapid chain rusting if lubrication is skipped. Electrical issues: RE bikes — especially older Bullet models — have notorious electrical gremlins. Self-start failures and indicator issues are common. Battery terminals corrode faster in Bengaluru's humidity. Vibrations at high RPM: Classic 350 and older models have inherent vibrations. If vibrations suddenly increase, it may indicate a loose engine mounting bolt or worn engine mounts. Overheating in traffic: RE's air-cooled engine needs moving air to cool efficiently. Extended Bengaluru traffic jams can cause heat soak — the oil temperature rises and oil effectiveness decreases. Short idling periods at junctions are fine, but try to avoid stationary idle for more than 15 minutes.
Royal Enfield Service Cost: Authorised Centre vs Fiixup

At an authorised Royal Enfield service centre in Bengaluru, expect to pay: Basic service (labour only) ₹600–₹800. Oil change (labour + RE Genuine Oil 15W-50 engine oil) ₹900–₹1,200. Full service with filters ₹1,500–₹2,500. Wait time: 4–8 hours minimum. Travel time: 30–60 minutes each way. At Fiixup's doorstep service: Basic service ₹349 (labour) + oil cost. Full service with genuine-grade 15W-50 oil: ₹699–₹899. No travel. No waiting. Service done in your parking in 1–1.5 hours. Warranty: 30 days. The cost difference is minimal but the time saving is 3–5 hours per visit.

For Royal Enfield bikes under warranty (first 5 years / 50,000 km), complete the mandatory first 3 services at an authorised centre to protect your warranty. For subsequent services, Fiixup's doorstep service using Royal Enfield-grade 15W-50 oil is a convenient and equally qualified alternative.

sections.content: The question we get asked most often: 'Is doorstep car service as good as a proper garage?' The answer, for most standard maintenance and repairs, is yes — and in many ways it's better. This is an honest, point-by-point comparison to help you decide.
Cost: Which Is Cheaper?

For identical work, doorstep service is typically 10–25% cheaper than traditional garages. Here's why: garages pay rent on prime commercial land, electricity for lifts and equipment, reception staff, and often commission agents who source customers. These costs are embedded in their labour charges. Mobile mechanics have lower overheads and pass the savings to customers. Additionally, you save towing costs if your car isn't driveable, and you save the time value of 3–4 hours spent at a garage — a significant cost for salaried professionals.
Quality: Is Doorstep Work Less Good?

Not for standard maintenance. Oil changes, filter replacements, brake pad fitting, battery service, tyre puncture repair, and AC re-gassing are all equally well-performed at your doorstep as in a garage — the tools and materials are identical. For very complex jobs — full engine rebuilds, gearbox replacement, structural body repair — a specialist workshop with a vehicle lift is genuinely better suited. A good doorstep service will tell you honestly when a job exceeds what's safe to do at your location.
Convenience: No Contest

In Bengaluru, a typical garage visit costs 2–3 hours minimum: 45–60 minutes travel each way in traffic, 30–60 minutes waiting time, and the service itself. Many garages don't guarantee same-day completion — leaving your car overnight is common. Doorstep service eliminates all of this. The mechanic comes to you in 30–60 minutes, works while you're home or at your desk, and your car is back within hours — often less than 2 hours for common services. You also don't need to arrange transport while your car is at the garage.
Transparency: The Biggest Advantage of Doorstep

When you leave your car at a garage, you have zero visibility into what's being done. Are the parts they charged you for actually being fitted? Is the oil they're using the grade you paid for? Are there any 'extra' issues they're creating to upsell? With doorstep service, the mechanic works in front of you. You can see every part removed, every part fitted. You can ask questions and get immediate answers. This transparency eliminates the trust deficit that plagues traditional garages.
Parts: Genuine vs Aftermarket

Both garages and mobile services can use genuine OEM parts or quality aftermarket alternatives. At Fiixup, we carry OEM-grade parts for common services and source specific genuine parts on request. The key difference: we show you the part before fitting and document it on the invoice. No garage does this as standard.
Warranty: What You Get

Fiixup provides a 30-day warranty on all services — if any covered issue recurs within 30 days, we fix it free of charge. Many local garages provide no written warranty at all. Authorised service centres provide 3-month warranties but at 2–4x the cost.

For most car owners in Bengaluru and Chennai, the smart approach is: use Fiixup's doorstep service for all regular maintenance (oil change, filters, brakes, battery, AC), and only visit an authorised centre for warranty claims or very complex repairs.
